title: QQ Sparse Random Completion v1 implementation
objective: Compile arbitrary-width bounded and reciprocal-uniform 1/n dense QQ random_matrix generation directly into one owned FmpqMatrix resource call, preserving seeded and fallback semantics with competitive warm performance

handoff.summary: Dense QQ random_matrix compiles arbitrary-width bounded and Sage-compatible reciprocal-uniform 1/n generation into one source-transparent native generator call. The kernel allocates and fills a private FmpqMatrix without advancing the shared RNG on failure; the host then makes one read-only bulk copy into its FLINT/GMP allocator domain, closes the private source in its owner domain, and only then publishes the final RNG state and mutable matrix. Native-disabled exact serialization parity covers all four 200x300 workloads. Public regressions cover five seeds, collisions, integral bounds, wide/skewed bounds, 1/n, failed allocation, six repeated injected failures of sagejs.ffi.flint.fmpq_matrix_copy with exact RNG rollback, and greater-than-1000-bit public mutation followed by idempotent close. The retained clean-source linux-x64 report identifies commit 8436557, its Git tree, the 16-core AMD EPYC host, OS, Node runtime, and memory. Compiled 200x300 density=.2 warm medians were 2.46 ms for small bounds, 9.95 ms for 80/97-bit bounds, 10.84 ms for 17/521-bit skew, and 2.41 ms for 1/n, versus SageMath medians of 1.77, 4.47, 3.76, and 1.33 ms. The 1000x1000 density=.1 wide case was 104.68 ms versus SageMath 50.73 ms. A fresh build preceded current-HEAD focused, architecture, strict, portable, and complete native receipts.
risks: The ownership boundary requires one matrix-area FLINT deep copy after native generation. The retained timing and memory evidence includes that copy, but it increases transient memory and is O(rows*columns), including structural zero entries.

A generated resource's type identity does not imply allocator interchangeability. Future code must preserve owner dispatch for allocation-growing mutation and destruction, or repeat this private-result-to-host-copy publication pattern; publishing the private token directly would reintroduce cross-addon FLINT/GMP lifetime corruption.

The sanitizer harness validates 200 rounds of the read-only deep-copy, source-close, large-limb destination mutation, and destination-close lifetime sequence through the adapter primitives available in one process. It deliberately does not claim to instantiate two separately linked allocator domains; the public subprocess regression exercises the actual generated-addon-to-host publication boundary.
The retained benchmark is linux-x64 evidence. Windows x64, macOS arm64, and linux arm64 rely on the same-source fallback and declared FLINT resource machinery but still need platform CI evidence.

Each selected rational still calls declared fmpq_matrix_set_entry inside the isolated core. This has no host crossings and scales with selected entries, but future bulk FLINT APIs may reduce per-entry retained-byte accounting overhead further.
next_steps: Run the retained benchmark and native lifecycle regression on macOS arm64, linux arm64, and Windows x64 before integration.
Consider explicit resource-owner dispatch in the generated FFI runtime so a private variable-size resource can remain mutable without a publication copy.
Integrate this lane after independent review and reuse the documented allocator-provenance rule for other generated variable-size resources.
